mechanism_narrative: The level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 20-day forward returns: lower rates reduce the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, increasing equity valuations and leading to positive returns. The relationship is monotonic and holds across the observed rate range.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 1.5% is associated with negative 20-day returns (p<0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in CPIAUCSL above 0.3% signals inflationary pressure that triggers central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% in 1 month, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances (p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment is low (UNRATE < 4.5%) and consumer spending is strong (RSAFS > 380000), the economy is in a strong growth phase, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In instances where UNRATE < 4.5% and RSAFS > 380000, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases (p>0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: In the late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDPC1 annualized growth > 2% and UNRATE < 4.5%), the economy is overheating, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth > 2% and UNRATE < 4.5%), the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances (p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: The level of industrial production (INDPRO) is positively related to S&P 500 20-day forward returns: higher industrial production signals strong economic activity, increasing equity valuations and leading to positive returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO above 115 is associated with negative 20-day returns (p<0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.5%) signals economic weakness and recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 5.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances (p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 3.0% signals a monetary tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 3.0%, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances (p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.5%) signals economic weakness and recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 5.5%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances (p>0.05 for negative returns).
